title: Police’s Handling of Voyeurism Cases and Issuance of Conditional Warning
what_it_is: Police’s Handling of Voyeurism Cases and Issuance of Conditional Warning

sections.label: Campus sexual harassment questions
sections.summary: Questions asked the Minister for Home Affairs on campus sexual harassment reports, warnings, prosecutions, conditional warnings and a public education campaign.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) for each year from 2008, how many cases of campus sexual harassment and sexual assault at autonomous universities were reported to the Police; (b) of these, how many resulted in warnings and how many resulted in criminal prosecution; and (c) what were the considerations behind determining the nature of the action taken in such cases.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs in light of the Police report made by an NUS student against a person who took a video-recording of her in the bathroom (a) how do the Police assess whether a person should be given a conditional warning; (b) what percentage of suspects given a conditional warning in similar cases have been rehabilitated; (c) what percentage of suspects went on to re-offend; and (d) whether there is any review of this practice after this case has been discussed widely.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs whether the Ministry will consider a public education campaign where people are educated not to watch or circulate voyeur videos or photos even if they do not contain nudity but which sexualise young people without their consent.

sections.label: Sexual misconduct cases in universities
sections.summary: MOE told Parliament that from AY2015/2016 to AY2017/2018, 56 sexual misconduct cases were reported to AUs and 37 to Police.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Earlier, the Ministry of Education had informed Parliament that from Academic Year (AY) 2015/2016 to AY2017/2018, 56 cases of sexual misconduct were reported to the AUs and 37 of these cases were reported to the Police.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: There was insufficient evidence to make out offences in two cases, and investigations in another four cases are ongoing.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Of the remaining 31 cases, 16 were prosecuted in Court.

sections.label: Re-offender jailed and fined
sections.summary: He re-offended in 2017 and was prosecuted for his 2015 and 2017 offences, jailed eight months and fined S$2,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: He re-offended in 2017, and the Police prosecuted him in Court for both his 2015 and 2017 offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: He was sent to jail for eight months and fined S$2,000.

sections.label: Proposed sexual offence laws
sections.summary: New offences were proposed for sexual exploitation of minors, voyeurism, distribution of intimate images and cyber-flashing.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We have proposed new offences to deal with sexual exploitation of minors.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We have also proposed new standalone offences for voyeurism, distribution of intimate images, commonly known as "revenge pornography"; and sexual exposure over the Internet, commonly known as "cyber-flashing".

sections.label: Charges withdrawn, conditional warning given
sections.summary: AGC directed Police to withdraw the charges and he was given a 24-month conditional warning.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In the end, AGC directed the Police to withdraw the charges and he was given a 24-month conditional warning.

sections.label: Public perception of safety survey
sections.summary: The 2018 Public Perception Survey found 93% of locals felt safe, with 87% of women feeling safe in their neighbourhood.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Based on the Police's 2018 Public Perception Survey, the perception of overall safety and security in Singapore among locals was 93%.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Specifically, women and their perception of safety in their neighbourhood – 87% – nearly nine in 10 feel safe in their neighhourhood.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Seventy-four percent of women feel safe walking alone in their neighbourhood at night.

sections.label: Men jailed for voyeurism videos
sections.summary: Five men were jailed between six months and three years for serial voyeurism and sharing videos of victims online.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Another illustration: five men were jailed between six months and three years for engaging in serial acts of voyeurism and sharing videos of their victims in an online forum.

sections.label: Nicholas Lim conditional warning terms
sections.summary: Mr Nicholas Lim will be charged for the Monica Baey offence and any new offence if he offends within 12 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Mr Nicholas Lim is on thin ice with his conditional warning.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If he offends within the period of 12 months, he will be charged for the offence relating to Ms Monica Baey and the new offence.

sections.label: One warned student re-offended
sections.summary: Of 15 who received warnings, one student re-offended and was jailed.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Out of the 15 who received warnings, one student re-offended, and he was dealt with severely; he went to jail.

sections.label: Sexual crime officers and OneSafe Centre
sections.summary: Specialist investigation officers and the OneSafe Centre let rape victims undergo interviews and forensic examinations at one private location.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We have trained a group of specialist investigation officers to handle sexual crime cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We have rolled out the One-Stop Abuse Forensic Examination (OneSafe) Centre, where victims of rape can undergo interviews and forensic medical examinations at a single private location without having to go between the Police station and the hospital.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah asked if we would consider a public education campaign about the harms of taking and distributing voyeuristic videos.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We certainly will, but I think a very good public education campaign will be if Parliament passes the amendments later today.

sections.label: Police assessment by officers
sections.summary: The investigating officers and their superiors make the Police assessment.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The investigating officers and their superiors make the Police assessment.

sections.label: AGC makes final decision
sections.summary: Trained officers make an assessment, discussed with the AGC, which makes the final decision using the legal framework and factors.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But these are highly trained officers who do this every day; they make an assessment.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: That is then discussed with the AGC, which makes the final decision, taking into account the legal framework and the overall set of factors.

sections.label: Tough on crime stance
sections.summary: The passage states there was never any intention or practice of being soft, citing amendments to the Penal Code.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We have made that an article of faith that we are tough.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We are tough on crime, we are tough on the causes of crime and, as the fact that we are putting up amendments to the Penal Code shows, there was never any intention and never any practice of being soft.

sections.label: Impact on victims
sections.summary: The passage states that the impact on the victims is very important.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The impact on the victims is very important.

sections.label: Consistency in similar cases
sections.summary: The passage states fairness requires similar outcomes in two cases with a similar set of facts, for consistency.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: You then have another case, with a similar set of facts.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I think fairness requires that, in both cases, the outcome is similar, so that there is consistency.
